messages.subject: Debugging issues in running examples
parts:
Greetings,

First, many thanks for the RHIPE package and for the help contributed
on this forum. I've been banging my head against the wall to get
through a series of errors, and now I'm stuck on some examples from
the guide and from this forum.

In particular, I keep hitting the same errors from Hadoop. The logs
from the Hadoop jobtracker are below (for experiment 2). I've tried a
bunch of different "experiments", to test all the bases that I could
think of.

In experiment 1, the commands were:
rhwrite(list(1,2,3),"/tmp/test")
rhread("/tmp/test")

This works as expected, with the following excerpt:

Wrote 3 pairs occupying 57 bytes
[1] TRUE
> rhread("/tmp/test")
RHIPE: Read 3 pairs occupying 57 bytes, deserializing
[[1]]
[[1]][[1]]
[1] "1"
...


In experiment 2, the commands were:

In bash:
export HADOOP=/usr/lib/hadoop-0.20
export HADOOP_BIN=/usr/lib/hadoop-0.20/bin

R
rhoptions(runner = c("/general/installed/bin/R","CMD", rhoptions()
$runner))
library(Rhipe)
rhinit(TRUE,TRUE,buglevel=2000)
rhoptions(runner = c("/general/installed/bin/R","CMD", rhoptions()
$runner))
z=rhmr(map=expression(), N=3, inout=c("lapp","seq"),ifolder="/tmp/
x", mapred=list(mapred.reduce.tasks=0, mapred.reduce.max.attempts=1,
mapred.map.max.attempts=1))
rhex(z)


Result: the error logs are below. Within R, the following error
was produced:
11/03/14 15:05:33 INFO mapred.JobClient: Failed map
tasks=1
result:256
Error in readBin(f1, "raw", f2) : invalid 'n' argument

Experiment 3:
I tried the following example:

map <- expression({
lapply(seq_along(map.values),function(r){
x <- runif(map.values[[r]])

rhcollect(map.keys[[r]],c(n=map.values[[r]],mean=mean(x),sd=sd(x)))
})
})

z <- rhmr(map, ofolder="/tmp/test",
inout=c('lapply','sequence'),
N=10,mapred=list(mapred.reduce.tasks=0,
mapred.reduce.max.attempts=1, mapred.map.max.attempts=1,
mapred.job.queue.name='interactive'),jobname='test')

rhex(z)

The resulting errors were the same.

Experiment 4:
This was motivated by a comment elsewhere on the forum
Command: R CMD /general/installed/R-2.12.1-acml/lib64/R/library/
Rhipe/libs/imperious.so
Result: Segmentation fault

Experiment 5:
I looked at ldd on imperious.so, and the results were the same for
the local and compute nodes. The Hadoop installation I'm using
doesn't have local jobtrackers enabled, so I couldn't test whether
things run locally.


I think I've been over everything, but I can't figure out the issue.
I've tried versions 0.65.1 (at least the patched version cited in a
link in another thread), 0.65.2, and 0.65.3.

I've seen online that mapred.input.file == null should possibly be
replaced with map.input.file = NULL, but I see no reason why this
should be a stumbling block for me, when others have had success with
RHIPE. So, is there something I'm missing?

Thanks!

David

Cheers
Saptarshi

messages.author: 76174213f7be4102
messages.subject: Re: Debugging issues in running examples
parts:
This was the key, thanks!

The key was adding the LD_LIBRARY_PATH. For the benefit of others
happening by, my steps were:

1: Get the output of: rhoptions$runner[1] # /general/installed/
R-2.12.1-acml/lib64/R/library/Rhipe/libs/imperious.so

2: At the command line, run: ldd /general/installed/R-2.12.1-acml/
lib64/R/library/Rhipe/libs/imperious.so

3: I took all of the unique directories listed from LDD results and
added them to the LD_LIBRARY_PATH string.
I now create a special list/string, called str_LD_LIBRARY_PATH
(like the "mapred" list variable you suggested),
to make this easy to generalize, and included R libraries, for
good measure, e.g.:

str_LD_LIBRARY_PATH = list( LD_LIBRARY_PATH= "/usr/lib64:/lib64:/
general/installed/lib:/general/installed/R-2.12.1-acml/lib64")

This then passed via rhmr as you suggested:

user/david/rhipe0315a",
mapred=append(str_LD_LIBRARY_PATH,list(mapred.map.tasks=2,mapred.reduce.tasks=0)))

This matched your suggestion and seems to have worked perfectly.
All of my other little tests work, too, thanks!

David
